items.prompt:
Comparing two things to explain one (body is like a thermostat) is an:
A) analogy
B) category
C) rhyme

Sorting energy into renewable and nonrenewable uses:
A) categories
B) rhyme
C) a flashback

'Unlike the first leader, the second...' signals a:
A) distinction/contrast
B) rhyme
C) summary

Read.

Like a thermostat, the body senses heat and triggers sweating to cool down.

The author uses an analogy to:
A) explain how the body regulates temperature
B) list ingredients
C) tell a story
items.answer: A) explain how the body regulates temperature

solution.answer: A) explain how the body regulates temperature

items.prompt:
Read.

The text groups energy into renewable (solar, wind) and nonrenewable (coal, oil).

This organizes ideas by:
A) categories
B) rhyme
C) chronology only

Read.

Unlike the first president, who avoided parties, the second openly took sides.

The author draws a:
A) contrast between the two leaders
B) comparison showing they are identical
C) random fact
items.answer: A) contrast between the two leaders

steps: Shows a difference. Key is A.
solution.answer: A) contrast between the two leaders

items.prompt:
An author writes, 'A government's budget is like a household's: income must cover spending, or debt grows.' The MAIN purpose of this analogy is to:
A) explain a complex idea using a familiar one
B) confuse the reader
C) change the topic
items.answer: A) explain a complex idea using a familiar one

steps: Analogy aids understanding. Key is A.
solution.answer: A) explain a complex idea using a familiar one

items.prompt:
Why do authors use connections (comparisons, analogies) and distinctions (contrasts, categories)?
A) to help readers understand how ideas relate and differ
B) to fill space
C) to hide the main idea
items.answer: A) to help readers understand how ideas relate and differ

solution.answer: A) to help readers understand how ideas relate and differ
